source: DdsEQhNAyl4.mp4 (1080x1920, 60 fps container, 56.03 s; mpdecimate keeps ~32 unique frames/s in an 18-23 s sample, so the CG was likely rendered at 24-30 fps and frame-doubled)

reel.caption_cta: Comment "SHEET" for Free Access! (caption opens 'Based on a true story', ends 'made with higgsfield')

style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-54.52 s; hard cut into a 1.5 s live-action handheld phone 'real me' flex tag (54.52-56.03 s). Yellow word-by-word captions with black outline; green 'RESPECT.' caption over the tag. Top title caption in the first second.
logline: A broke teen reseller is thrown out by his dad with 30 days to prove himself; at rock bottom in the rain his phone starts dinging with sales, he scales from a stockroom to a giant warehouse, and when his dad turns up asking if he works there he says 'Nope. I own it.'

hook.mechanic: Title caption states the promise ('Daddy said I'd fail') over a confrontation already in progress: dad looms over the son's stock wall and mocks him in one long line, son's lame 'I'm a reseller!' and a cutting 'How many did you sell?' - followed by an awkward silent beat. Unlike most of this creator's reels the hook is ONE static 5.4 s wide shot, held on dialogue.
hook.first_line: Dad! / You're 30 years old, unemployed, and this is your plan?

montage.description: Wordless-ish hustle montage after 'Let's work!' (10 s, 13 shots, median 0.66 s; only 'Gotcha. / Bro...' spoken): tape boxes in a small stockroom as boxes drop in and wall up the frame, whip-pan to an iced-out watch display, repeated 'photograph into the lens with a flash' match cuts with ever-bigger piles of stock in front, juggling tape rolls, then match cuts to the same taping pose in bigger and bigger warehouses (sped-up), a conveyor line and a time-lapse aisle, ending back on the boxes walling up the lens. A shorter failure montage (shots 5-21, 10.97-16.00 s) sets this up: same 'hold up a shirt to camera' pose match-cut across six shirts with one-word reactions ('Nothing', 'Okay?', 'Cool', 'Awesome').

stats.dead_air: None in the audio sense: a music/SFX bed runs the full 56 s (silencedetect -35 dB/0.4 s found no silence). Gaps with no dialogue (>=1.5 s): 13.70-17.42 (3.7 s), 18.72-20.44 (1.7 s), 28.52-30.34 (1.8 s), 32.28-37.17 (4.9 s), 38.31-44.00 (5.7 s), 45.60-48.10 (2.5 s), 54.47-56.03 (1.6 s).

beats.summary: HOOK: dad mocks the son's reselling stock wall; 'How many did you sell?' - silence.
Kicked out: dad throws his bags out the door; nose-to-nose bargain - 'Give me one month' / 'You have 30 days'; door shuts, he's alone on the porch.
Failure montage: laptop, product photos with flash, six shirts held to camera with one-word reactions, sleeping on his bin bags, more photos and listings.
Rock bottom: thrown into a rainy street, slumped against his stock as dad's '30 days' echoes - 'Maybe he was right.' Phone buzzes: 'Wait... no, wait... Yo!'
Turn: frantic packing, phone dings non-stop, crash zoom into his eye, store page shows everything sold - 'All of it.'
'Let's work!' - doors open onto sunshine; hustle montage from stockroom to huge warehouse.

Reversal: dad pulls up at the warehouse in an old pickup - 'Nate? You work here?' Doors open on the vast operation. 'Nope. I own it.' Dad's face in snap-zoom ECU: 'What? There's no way you made all this.'
Meta punchline/CTA: Nate turns to camera - 'I made this video. Link in bio.'
Real-me tag: 5 handheld live-action flex clips (real warehouse, supercars, LED lounge, luxury van, iced watch) under 'RESPECT.'

transcription: faster-whisper small (CPU, int8), word timestamps; cross-checked against burned-in captions in 0.1-0.2 s strips. 'Nate?' (x2) and 'Yo!' corrected from captions.
why_it_works: Title caption 'Daddy said I'd fail' plants the payoff in frame 1, so every humiliation reads as setup for revenge.
The hook breaks the house pattern: a single held wide with fast, cruel dialogue, ending on an unanswered question and a silent beat - the silence is the joke.
Clear ticking clock ('You have 30 days'), said face to face in an extreme close-up profile two-shot, then echoed as V.O. at rock bottom.
Failure is played as comedy (six match-cut shirts, one-word deadpan reactions, sleeping on bin bags, slapstick dive into a puddle), which keeps a sad stretch watchable.
Lighting does the storytelling: night, rain and screen-glow for the low point; first daylight (bright blue sky) exactly on 'Let's work!'; cool high-key warehouse for success.
The turn is sound-led and escalates: phone dings stack up while a slow push accelerates into a crash zoom into his pupil.
Montage uses 'same pose, bigger world' match cuts (photo flash, taping) plus boxes walling up the lens as a wipe, so scale grows without words.
The reveal is staged with a door-opening OTS and a deep symmetrical wide that makes Nate tiny in a huge space; the dad's reaction gets a snap zoom into a cartoon ECU.
Line economy: the win is two words ('Nope. I own it.'), and the ending turns meta ('I made this video. Link in bio.') into a direct CTA that matches the 'Comment SHEET' caption.
1.5 s real-life flex tag under a one-word caption grounds the fable in the creator's own life and makes the loop feel like a flex rather than an ending.
undetermined: Music not identified; a music/SFX bed runs under the whole reel (silencedetect -35 dB / 0.4 s found no silence).
'Nate?' at 44.0 s and the second 'Nate?' at 48.1-48.7 s come from captions only; whisper stretched 'You work here?' across 38.9-45.6 s. Timings estimated from caption changes.
'Yo!' (24.28 s) is from the caption; whisper heard 'Go!'.
'Ding, ding...' (26.94-27.86) is probably the phone notification sound (or the boy mimicking it); counted in words_total, which inflates words/s slightly (without it: 5 fewer words).
Captions show 'How you even make it'; whisper has 'How did you even make it?' - kept whisper.

Shot 30 and shot 42 contain an in-shot 'boxes wall up the lens' move that could be read as an extra cut; counted as one shot each. Speaker split of short lines in shots 2-3 inferred from mouth movement and staging.
Shot 23 (6.9 s) checked frame by frame: one continuous locked-off wide with a very slight drift in, no hidden cut.
